newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent to pause under upside cap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent to pause under upside cap.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+Tuesday's attempt to fill the gap from $18.62-$18.77 failed and this gap has taken the shape of a large bear, looming above the market.
+Next strong support will be found at $17.61 a barrel, the level of recent lows.
+Gas oil is supported at $161.75 but stronger support lies at around $160.
IPE Brent crude oil futures have lost their bullish bias and traders and technical analysts expect the market to be capped to the upside on Wednesday.
June Brent closed 35 cents down on the day at $17.99 a barrel, after earlier reaching a high of $18.64, peeping into a gap formed earlier on the June contract chart between $18.62 and $18.77.
June Brent was quoted at $18.10 a barrel in Singapore ahead of the London open.
Gas oil nudged 50 cents higher than the previous resistance level to touch $167, before settling back to close $1.50 lower at $163.75.
"The technical patterns are now negative," said Steve Kwan at MMS in London. "Although it may trade slightly higher this morning people do not have confidence now after yesterday's sharp down move."
"It will not be very wise to buy rallies...upticks will be an opportunity to sell."
"The gap to $18.77 remains open and for the market to turn bullish again we will have to fill that gap."
He said that the low point of the year, reached on April 17, would be the next important layer of support.
MeesPierson Derivatives in London, using their Market Profile technique, said they expected Brent to trade within the parameters of Tuesday's trade but adopted a slightly more positive stance.
"Today the range is clear, $18 to $18.24/$18.32 and then $18.24/32 to $18.64," their daily report said.
Gas oil was supported at $163.50 and $163.00, the report added, and pegged resistance at $164.50, $165.25 ad $167.
